## Declarations and implementations

```plato
//==
// # Constants
//
// Named constant values: irrational and derived numbers, angle-related scalars,
// unit-conversion factors, axis vectors, and canonical unit shapes.
//
// Constants dispatch on an ignored receiver of the result type (`Pi(_: Number)`),
// matching the intrinsic constants in `intrinsics.library.plato`
// and the `Identity(_: Quaternion)` family in
// `transforms.library.plato`. Read them
// as `Number.GoldenRatio`, `Vector3D.UnitZ`, `Circle.UnitCircle`.
//
// `Pi`, `Tau`, `E`, `Epsilon`, `MinValue`, `MaxValue`, `Zero`, `One` and
// `MinusOne` are NOT redeclared here — they are intrinsics
//      (`intrinsics.library.plato`) or derived in the `core-*` /
//      `algebra-*` libraries.

library Constants
{
    //==
    // Irrational and derived numeric constants

    // The golden ratio (1 + sqrt 5) / 2, approximately 1.618034.
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_ratio)
    GoldenRatio(_: Number): Number
        => (1.0 + 5.0.Sqrt) / 2.0;

    // Conventional name for the golden ratio.
    Phi(_: Number): Number
        => Number.GoldenRatio;

    // The reciprocal of the golden ratio, approximately 0.618034. Equal to
    // Phi - 1.
    RPhi(_: Number): Number
        => 1.0 / Number.Phi;

    // The square root of two, approximately 1.414214.
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Square_root_of_2)
    SqrtTwo(_: Number): Number
        => 1.4142135623730951;

    // The square root of three, approximately 1.732051.
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Square_root_of_3)
    SqrtThree(_: Number): Number
        => 1.7320508075688772;

    // The square root of five, approximately 2.236068.
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Square_root_of_5)
    SqrtFive(_: Number): Number
        => 2.23606797749979;

    // The natural logarithm of ten, approximately 2.302585.
    Ln10(_: Number): Number
        => 2.302585092994046;

    // The natural logarithm of two, approximately 0.693147.
    Ln2(_: Number): Number
        => 0.6931471805599453;

    // The base-ten logarithm of e, approximately 0.434294.
    Log10E(_: Number): Number
        => 0.4342944819032518;

    //==
    // Angle-related scalars
    //
    // These are raw Numbers, not Angles: they are conversion factors and
    // radian magnitudes used to build Angle values (see `angles.library.plato`),
    // not angles in their own right.

    // Two pi: the number of radians in a full turn. Spelled `Tau` as an
    // intrinsic; this is the conventional alternative name.
    TwoPi(_: Number): Number
        => Number.Tau;

    // Half of pi: the number of radians in a quarter turn.
    HalfPi(_: Number): Number
        => Number.Pi / 2.0;

    // Radians per degree: multiply a degree count by this to get radians.
    RadiansPerDegree(_: Number): Number
        => Number.Pi / 180.0;

    // Degrees per radian: multiply a radian count by this to get degrees.
    DegreesPerRadian(_: Number): Number
        => 180.0 / Number.Pi;

    //==
    // Unit-conversion factors
    //
    // Each is named `<A>Per<B>`: the number of A in one B. Exact where the
    // definition is exact (pound, ounce, troy ounce, mile, ton).

    // Feet in one metre.
    FeetPerMeter(_: Number): Number
        => 3.280839895;

    // Feet in one statute mile (exact).
    FeetPerMile(_: Number): Number
        => 5280.0;

    // Kilograms in one avoirdupois pound (exact by definition).
    PoundPerKilogram(_: Number): Number
        => 0.45359237;

    // Pounds in one US short ton (exact).
    PoundPerTon(_: Number): Number
        => 2000.0;

    // Grams in one avoirdupois ounce (exact by definition).
    OuncePerGram(_: Number): Number
        => 28.349523125;

    // Grams in one troy ounce (exact by definition).
    TroyOuncePerGram(_: Number): Number
        => 31.1034768;

    // Mean days in a Gregorian calendar year.
    GregorianYearDays(_: Number): Number
        => 365.2425;

    //==
    // Axis vectors
    //
    // The standard basis. The dimension is carried by the receiver type, so these
    // read as `Vector3D.UnitX`, `Vector2D.UnitY`, and so on.

    // The 2D unit vector along +X: (1, 0).
    UnitX(_: Vector2D): Vector2D
        => Vector2D(1.0, 0.0);

    // The 2D unit vector along +Y: (0, 1).
    UnitY(_: Vector2D): Vector2D
        => Vector2D(0.0, 1.0);

    // The 3D unit vector along +X: (1, 0, 0).
    UnitX(_: Vector3D): Vector3D
        => Vector3D(1.0, 0.0, 0.0);

    // The 3D unit vector along +Y: (0, 1, 0).
    UnitY(_: Vector3D): Vector3D
        => Vector3D(0.0, 1.0, 0.0);

    // The 3D unit vector along +Z: (0, 0, 1).
    UnitZ(_: Vector3D): Vector3D
        => Vector3D(0.0, 0.0, 1.0);

    //==
    // Physical constants

    // Standard gravity: the conventional acceleration of free fall at the
    // Earth's surface, fixed by definition at exactly 9.80665 m/s^2 (CGPM 1901)
    // rather than measured -- local values vary with latitude and altitude.
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Standard_gravity)
    StandardGravity(_: Acceleration): Acceleration
        => new Acceleration(9.80665);
```
